title: Warnings Before You Hit the Limit
objectives: Understand what a near-cap warning means and why it triggers before you reach your limit.
Recognize what a low-balance warning means and how it helps prevent a declined payment.
Know what clear, plain-language action to take when you receive an alert.

analogy.title: Low-Fuel Light for Your Spending
analogy.text: Think of alerts like the low-fuel light on your car dashboard or the 20% battery warning on your phone. They don't mean you've stopped - they mean you should plan ahead. A near-cap alert is like seeing you have 50 miles left before empty; you can slow down or refuel soon. A low-balance alert is like your phone warning you to plug in before it shuts off. Both give you time to act calmly - add funds, adjust your cap, or pause spending - so you avoid an unexpected stop.

pitch30Seconds: Imagine never being surprised at checkout. Our alerts are calm, early warnings that you are close to your spending cap or your balance is running low. Instead of a sudden decline, you get time to act - add money to your account, adjust your cap, or wait on a purchase. It's about control and confidence. You stay in charge, avoid embarrassment at the register, and keep spending exactly where you want it.
keyPoints: A close-to-cap signal tells you you're approaching your spending limit and a purchase could be declined soon.
A running-low balance signal tells you funds are getting low and it's time to add money to avoid disruption.
When you get an alert, check your balance and cap, then add funds, adjust your cap, or pause spending.
Alerts use a calm, trustworthy tone to help you act early without alarm or confusion.

recallQuiz.question: What does a 'near your cap' alert mean?
options: You have exceeded your cap and your card is blocked
You are close to your spending limit and should review before your next purchase
recallQuiz.explanation: A near-cap alert is an early warning that you are approaching your limit, giving you time to adjust your cap or spending before a decline.

recallQuiz.question: What does a 'running low' balance alert mean?
options: Your spending cap has increased automatically
Your available funds are getting low and you may need to add money soon
recallQuiz.explanation: A low-balance alert tells you funds are running low so you can add money before a payment is declined.

recallQuiz.question: What is the best next step after you receive an alert?
options: Check your balance and cap, then add funds, adjust your cap, or pause spending
Share your password with someone to check for you
recallQuiz.explanation: Checking your balance and cap lets you take a calm, plain-language action — add money, adjust your cap, or wait — to stay in control.

testModeNote: In test mode, alerts work the same way using sample data so you can practice without affecting real funds.
